Treatment summary
Patient presneted following a low-speed collision in a parking lot with reported head
impact and subsequent headache, dizziness, and difficulty concentrating, consisetnt
with a concussion mechanism for this type of event. Over the course of eight visits,
the patient was managed with symptom monitoring, graded return-to-activity guidance,
and cognitive and vestibular rest recommendations. Treatment followed a typical
progression and tapered as symptoms steadily improved. Examination findings were
mixed: certain vestibular and balance measures showed deficits that support the
reported injury, while other neurological screening tests returned within normal
limits. The patient also mentioned a minor strain involving the same region several
years ago, which had fully resolved without lasting limitation and does not appear to
have contributed to the current presentation. Billing records reflect single,
appropriate charges for each service rendered without duplication. At the most recent
visit, the patient reported near-resolution of symptoms and was cleared for graduated
return to usual activities, with follow-up as needed.

  or the driver who reported it). attorney = a lawyer for the claimant or plaintiff.
  defense_attorney = a lawyer for the insurance company or defendant.
Organization "type" must be one of: repair_shop, clinic, law_firm, court, insurer, police, other.
"policy_numbers" = only values labeled as a policy number. A claim number is not a policy number.
"street" and "city" = the person's own home address, only if the page gives it. Never use the
address of a clinic, shop, firm or court for a person.
"loss_dates" = only a date that the page clearly gives as the date of the accident, crash, loss or
injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
